rules.forbidden_features: Marine Regions EEZ attributes and any World Bank/IMF shipping magnitude (model.FORBIDDEN_FEATURE_RULES); shipping enters as presence shares only (value above 0)
rules.climatology: cell rate shrunk to the region rate by exposure-weighted empirical Bayes (Marshall 1991); region rate for cells unseen in training, global rate for unseen regions (so under leave-one-region-out the climatology equals the global rate)
rules.cv: leave-one-week-out (blocks of 7 dates from the first) and leave-one-region-out (reporting boxes, 'other' included)
rules.d2: 1 - Poisson deviance(model) / deviance(baseline) on the out-of-fold predictions of both, rows all models predict
rules.gate: anomalies only when the full model beats the climatology: pooled week-CV D2 > 0 and > 0 in more than half of the week folds
rules.anomaly: Poisson two-sided p (twice the smaller tail) of the observed count against the week-CV expectation; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR < 0.01 over tested rows in calm weather (wind < 12 m/s)
rules.calm: wind_ms < 12 (GFS 10 m wind at 18 UTC for VIIRS, at the scene hour for radar)
rules.robust: flag_robust: the Poisson-BH flag that is also significant (BH q < 0.01 over the same family) under a negative binomial tail with alpha = the moment estimate of the overdispersion (Cameron and Trivedi 1990)
rules.poisson_fdr_valid: true only when the Pearson dispersion of the counts against the expectation is at most 1.5 (a rule of thumb of this project); otherwise the Poisson BH flags do not carry a 1 % false-discovery guarantee and flag_robust is the set to review

viirs.target: clear-sky lit vessel candidates per 1,000 km2 of clear searched sea, per cell-night (VIIRS DNB, all passes)

gate.rule: the full model beats the climatology out of sample: pooled leave-one-week-out D2 against the climatology above 0 and above 0 in more than half of the week folds

anomalies.control: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over the tested rows
anomalies.family: tested rows (exposure >= 25 km2) with a finite expectation in calm weather (wind_ms < 12 m/s)
anomalies.nb_check: negative binomial two-sided tail with alpha = overdispersion.nb_alpha, BH over the same family
anomalies.note: Pearson dispersion of the counts against the model's expectation is 3.82 (1 for Poisson): the Poisson p-values are too small, the BH 1 % false-discovery statement does not hold for flag, and flag_robust (also significant under the negative binomial tail) is the set to review.

radar.target: radar vessel candidates (high, medium) per 1,000 km2 of imaged AOI sea, per cell-scene (Sentinel-1C/1D)

gate.rule: the full model beats the climatology out of sample: pooled leave-one-week-out D2 against the climatology above 0 and above 0 in more than half of the week folds

anomalies.control: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over the tested rows
anomalies.family: tested rows (exposure >= 25 km2) with a finite expectation in calm weather (wind_ms < 12 m/s)
anomalies.nb_check: negative binomial two-sided tail with alpha = overdispersion.nb_alpha, BH over the same family
anomalies.note: Pearson dispersion of the counts against the model's expectation is 19.24 (1 for Poisson): the Poisson p-values are too small, the BH 1 % false-discovery statement does not hold for flag, and flag_robust (also significant under the negative binomial tail) is the set to review.

columns.night: local evening date (viirs) or UTC date (radar)
columns.exposure_km2: clear searched sea (viirs) or imaged AOI sea (radar) of the cell
columns.observed: count in the cell (NaN when not tested)
columns.expected: leave-one-week-out expected count of the full trees
columns.expected_rate_all_per_1000km2: rate of the full trees fitted on all tested rows, for every row
columns.p_two_sided, q_bh: two-sided p and its BH q over the family (NaN outside it)
columns.flag: high, low or none (none for every row when the gate did not pass)
columns.flag_robust: flag where the negative binomial check (q_bh_nb < 0.01) also holds, else none

sources.name: scikit-learn Poisson regression example (frequency with exposure as sample weight)
Marshall, R. J. (1991). Mapping disease and mortality rates using empirical Bayes estimators. Applied Statistics 40, 283-294
Friedman, J. H. (2001). Greedy function approximation: a gradient boosting machine. Annals of Statistics 29, 1189-1232
Breiman, L. (2001). Random forests. Machine Learning 45, 5-32 (permutation importance)
Benjamini, Y. and Hochberg, Y. (1995). Controlling the false discovery rate. JRSS B 57, 289-300
Cameron, A. C. and Trivedi, P. K. (1990). Regression-based tests for overdispersion in the Poisson model. Journal of Econometrics 46, 347-364
Inputs: ocean layers and their sources
Inputs: VIIRS lights and clear-sky counts

caveat: Ocean and weather layers describe the sea, not what any vessel does. Expected activity says where lit boats or radar candidates usually are, given the sea and the weather; a cell above or below it is a lead for review, not evidence. Dark = no AIS match. Not evidence of illegal activity. An activity anomaly is a difference between a count of detections in a cell and a model's expectation for that cell, night or pass. It is not a count of vessels and not evidence of wrongdoing: model error, weather, cloud, moonlight, fleet movements and the sensors' limits (unlit boats for VIIRS, small boats for radar) all produce it. A lead for review only.
